title: Variance knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the main idea of “Variance”?
options: It removes the need to understand types or runtime behavior.
`out` supports safe covariance for produced values, while `in` supports contravariance for consumed values; invariant types allow both directions.
It makes versioning, input validation, and testing unnecessary.
It means all Kotlin libraries and platform APIs behave identically.
questions.answer_key: `out` supports safe covariance for produced values, while `in` supports contravariance for consumed values; invariant types allow both directions.
questions.explanation: The reliable answer is grounded in the lesson’s main principle: `out` supports safe covariance for produced values, while `in` supports contravariance for consumed values; invariant types allow both directions. Review the example and one relevant edge case before moving on.

questions.prompt: Which learning/debugging practice is most reliable for “Variance”?
options: Use a minimal reproducible example, compare the actual result with the expected result, and check the target/version assumptions.
Change several unrelated parts at once and keep the result that looks plausible.
Ignore warnings and suppress failures before identifying the cause.
Assume the compiler or toolchain is broken without reducing the example.
questions.answer_key: Use a minimal reproducible example, compare the actual result with the expected result, and check the target/version assumptions.
questions.explanation: A minimal reproducible example and version-aware testing separate a real behavior from a mistaken assumption. Review the example and one relevant edge case before moving on.

questions.prompt: Which claim should a learner avoid when applying “Variance”?
options: Never inspect the official API reference for the selected target.
Treat draft or experimental features as universally stable.
Expose every internal implementation detail to every caller.
Variance removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.
questions.answer_key: Variance removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.
questions.explanation: The misconception to avoid is: Variance removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version. Review the example and one relevant edge case before moving on.
